sources.title: Human History Map civilization index
sources.note: Exact imported Pandyas identity, approximate 500 to 800 interval and separately indexed neighboring and later identities.

sources.title: Human History Map 500 CE borders
sources.note: Decoded first Pandyas geometry, coordinate hash, topology and named point tests against simultaneous Chola, Pallava and Simhala layers.

sources.title: Human History Map 600 CE borders
sources.note: Decoded snapshot proving the exact Pandyas feature is absent during the internal 600 to 700 coverage gap.

sources.title: Human History Map 700 CE borders
sources.note: Decoded second Pandyas geometry, coordinate hash, topology and point ownership among Pallava, Chalukya, Chera and Chola layers.

sources.title: Human History Map 800 CE borders
sources.note: Decoded handoff from exact id pandyas to the distinct pandya-state and pallava atlas records.

sources.title: Human History Map 900 CE borders
sources.note: Decoded continued pandya-state layer and separately labeled Sri Lankan and rival South Indian layers.

sources.title: Human History Map 1000 CE borders
sources.note: Decoded later Chola Empire assignment of Madurai and far southern test points after the separately carded Pandya state interval.

sources.title: Human History Map 1279 CE borders
sources.note: Decoded much later and separately indexed pandya-state-1279 geometry, which unlike this target contains Madurai.

sources.title: Tamil Nadu Open University, History of India up to 1206 CE
sources.note: Official university course synthesis of the revived Pandya sequence from Kadungon through Nedunjadaiyan, with conventional dates used only as approximate guides.

sources.title: Archaeological Survey of India, South India to about A.D. 1300
sources.note: Authoritative survey explaining the unusually heavy dependence of early Pandya history on bilingual copper plates and the growth of stone inscriptions after the sixth century.

sources.title: Archaeological Survey of India, Epigraphia Indica XVII: Velvikudi grant
sources.note: Original scholarly edition, facsimile and translation of the Velvikudi grant, including royal genealogy, Kalabhra narrative, petition and land restoration.

sources.title: R. C. Majumdar, The Classical Age: Dynasties of South India
sources.note: Major scholarly synthesis stressing that early medieval Pandya genealogy and chronology remain unsettled while offering a provisional ruler sequence.

sources.title: R. C. Majumdar, The Age of Imperial Kanauj: South India
sources.note: Scholarly history of early Pandya rulers, campaigns and rivals based primarily on the Velvikudi and Sinnamanur records.

sources.title: IGNOU, State in Early Medieval India
sources.note: University synthesis of Pandya state formation, nadu and nattar institutions, brahmadeya and temple integration, revenue and limits of older political models.

sources.title: IGNOU, Early Medieval Economy and its Continuities
sources.note: University synthesis of sixth to tenth-century Pandya agrarian change, Tamraparni and Vaigai valleys, land controllers, peasants and labor.

sources.title: DHARMA, Velvikudi grant of Nedunjadaiyan, year 3
sources.note: Critical digital edition of the bilingual grant, its Grantha Sanskrit and Vatteluttu Tamil, regnal context and royal Sanskrit verse used for the written sample.

sources.title: DHARMA, SII 14.1 and 14.2: Anaimalai inscriptions
sources.note: Critical digital edition of dated Grantha and Vatteluttu records for the Narasimha cave, minister Maran Kari and his brother and successor Maran Eyinan.

sources.title: DHARMA, SII 14.3: Tirupparankunram inscription
sources.note: Critical digital edition of a year-six Vatteluttu record naming a shrine, tank, royal mahāsāmanta Sattan Ganapati and shrines built by Nakkan Korri.

sources.title: Tamil Nadu Archaeology, Ladan Koil at Anaimalai
sources.note: Official monument description of an eighth-century early Pandya rock-cut Murugan shrine, seated figures, pillars and sculptural details.

sources.title: Tamil Nadu Archaeology, Pandiyan Kalvettu Padukai
sources.note: Official account of an eighth-century Tamil verse inscription recording a chief, his son, a stonemason, a tank, stone facing, sluice and irrigated land.

sources.title: Tamil Nadu Archaeology, Inscriptions in Vatteluttu script
sources.note: Official script overview illustrating seventh-century Pandya irrigation and eighth-century donative inscriptions in the southern cursive script.

sources.title: Tamil Nadu Archaeology, Copper Plate Inscriptions
sources.note: Official description of Pandya seventh to tenth-century copper charters, Vatteluttu Tamil, Grantha Sanskrit, ring-bound plates and chance discoveries.

sources.title: Tamil Nadu Archaeology, Korkai excavation
sources.note: Official excavation page for the ancient Pandya port, brick structure, three probable soakage jars and clearly earlier Tamil-Brahmi material.

sources.title: Tamil Nadu Archaeology, The Cultural Heritage of Tamil Nadu
sources.note: Official archaeological survey of Korkai finds and their broad dating, including medieval ring features and earlier pottery, beads, bangles and ornaments.

sources.title: Government Museum Chennai, Pandya coins
sources.note: Official museum overview distinguishing early square coinage from the single or paired fish emblems common on seventh to tenth-century Pandya coins.

sources.title: IGNOU, Historical Background: The Bhakti Millennium
sources.note: University account of sixth to ninth-century Tamil Alvar and Nayanar devotion, Tamil composition, diverse participants and women.

sources.title: IGNOU, Medieval Society: Tamil Bhakti
sources.note: University discussion of Tamil devotional hymns, temple worship, pilgrimage, music-like poetic forms and social inclusion with continuing hierarchy.

sources.title: Heritage University of Kerala Journal, Jainism in the Tamil region
sources.note: Peer-reviewed study of eighth and ninth-century Jain teachers, images, patrons and continuing communities in the Pandya region.

sources.title: Samuel Beal, Buddhist Records of the Western World, volume 2
sources.note: Primary travel-record translation used cautiously for the mid-seventh-century secondhand account of Malakuta, commerce, pearls and religious conditions.

sources.title: R. C. Majumdar, The Classical Age: Trade
sources.note: Scholarly synthesis identifying Korkai and Saliyur as Pandya ports and describing coastal and river exchange in late ancient South India.

sources.title: Asia-Pacific Conference on Underwater Cultural Heritage, Tamiraparani ports
sources.note: Specialist archaeological summary distinguishing early historic Korkai from medieval Kayal and emphasizing changing delta routes and port networks.

sources.title: Anatomy in ancient India: a focus on the Susruta Samhita
sources.note: Peer-reviewed overview of early Indian medical learning and surgery, with explicit uncertainty about textual dates and no claim of local Pandya clinical access.

sources.title: ISEAS, Engineering Expansion: The Chola Invasion of Sri Lanka
sources.note: Research paper placing major Pandya-Anuradhapura warfare in the ninth-century context and explaining shifting Pallava, Pandya and Sri Lankan alignments.

sources.title: Monica L. Smith, Territories, corridors, and networks
sources.note: Archaeological model explaining why premodern states often worked through nodes, corridors and uneven influence rather than fixed surveyed borders.

sources.title: Government of Maharashtra Gazetteers, History: Chalukyas and Pandyas
sources.note: Government scholarly history discussing the Velvikudi report of the Venbai campaign and a Ganga marriage connection under late Chalukya conditions.

sources.title: IGNOU, Early Tamil Society: Regions and Cultures
sources.note: University synthesis of earlier Tamil wet and dry landscapes, rice, millet, animal work and tank irrigation, used only as inherited regional background with date limits.

proposedOverrides.summary: The early medieval Pandya revival, preserved in difficult charters and cave inscriptions while the atlas omits Madurai and a full century of geometry.

batchIdentityNotes: Exact target pandyas is indexed approximately 500 to 800 CE and was missing both a card and a researched override at initial audit.
Only world-500 and world-700 contain the exact target. The absent world-600 feature creates a real 600 to 700 geometry gap inside the indexed lifetime.
The 500 target is one Polygon, one ring and 16 positions with SHA-256 423f9dbbc4e92aca80118dd8aba45f9ecb8855d9ef5c63a8b27ea0b2fbf724af.
The 700 target is one Polygon, one ring and 19 positions with SHA-256 9c968604690830ee30a27d7ebd055374e30faa9784f9478a58941d0452f7ba51.
Both target polygons contain Korkai, Tirunelveli and Kanyakumari but exclude Madurai, Rameswaram, Dindigul, Karur, Uraiyur, Puhar, Kanchipuram, Kerala ports and all tested Sri Lankan points.
At 500 and 700 the atlas assigns Madurai to chola-empire; other nearby points move among pallavas, chalukyas, cheras and chola-empire. Simhala remains a separate island layer.
At 800 the exact target disappears and the distinct pandya-state record begins. pandya-state-1279 is a separate much later record whose geometry finally includes Madurai.
No appliesTo alias is added. The override leaves fell null and links pandya-state only as the next separately carded atlas and dynastic phase.
